items.descriptionOriginal: Τρίωρη παναττική στάση εργασίας από τις 8:00 έως τις 11:00 σήμερα, Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου, έχει ανακοινώσει η ΟΛΜΕ , καλώντας τις ΕΛΜΕ, τους εκπαιδευτικούς και όλα τα σωματεία να εκφράσουν έμπρακτα την αλληλεγγύη τους στους διωκόμενους συναδέλφους. Το Δ.Σ. της ΟΛΜΕ καταγγέλλει την πειθαρχική δίωξη των εκπαιδευτικών Δημήτρη Χαρτζουλάκη και Χρύσας Χοτζόγλου, οι οποίοι καλούνται σήμερα, Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου, ενώπιον του Πειθαρχικού Συμβουλίου. Σύμφωνα με την Ομοσπονδία, οι κατηγορίες που αντιμετωπίζουν ενδέχεται να οδηγήσουν ακόμη και στην οριστική παύση, δηλαδή στην απόλυσή τους. Συγκέντρωση στις 9:30 στην Περιφερειακή Διεύθυνση Εκπαίδευσης Αττικής Η κινητοποίηση πραγματοποιείται σήμερα, την ώρα εξέτασης της πειθαρχικής υπόθεσης, στις 9:30, στην Περιφερειακή Διεύθυνση Εκπαίδευσης Αττικής, στην οδό Ξενίας 24, κοντά στον σταθμό του μετρό «Μέγαρο Μουσικής». Η ΟΛΜΕ καλεί τους εκπαιδευτικούς και τα σωματεία να συμμετάσχουν στην κινητοποίηση, εκφράζοντας την αλληλεγγύη τους στους δύο συναδέλφους. Ολόκληρη η ανακοίνωση της ΟΛΜΕ: Το Δ.Σ. της ΟΛΜΕ καταγγέλλει την απαράδεκτη πειθαρχική δίωξη των συναδέλφων Δημήτρη Χαρτζουλάκη και Χρύσας Χοτζόγλου, οι οποίοι την Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου καλούνται ενώπιον του Πειθαρχικού Συμβουλίου, με κατηγορίες που μπορούν να οδηγήσουν ακόμα και στην ποινή της οριστικής παύσης, δηλαδή της απόλυσης. Οι δύο συνάδελφοι διώκονται για τη συνδικαλιστική τους δράση και συγκεκριμένα για τη συμμετοχή τους σε κινητοποίηση ενάντια στην αξιολόγηση σε σχολείο του Πειραιά. Υπενθυμίζουμε ότι στις 29 Απριλίου το Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο απέρριψε ομόφωνα την επιβολή δυνητικής αργίας στους δύο συναδέλφους, ενώ η Χρύσα Χοτζόγλου επέστρεψε στο σχολείο της έπειτα από 18 μήνες δυνητικής αργίας. Η εξέλιξη αυτή, όπως και άλλες πρόσφατες δικαιώσεις διωκόμενων εκπαιδευτικών, αναδεικνύει τη σημασία της συλλογικής δράσης και της αλληλεγγύης των ίδιων των συναδέλφων/συναδελφισσών, της ΕΛΜΕ Πειραιά, των ΕΛΜΕ και της Ομοσπονδίας. Η ποινικοποίηση της συνδικαλιστικής δράσης, οι διώξεις και τα πειθαρχικά δεν θα περάσουν! Σε μια περίοδο που οι εκπαιδευτικοί αντιμετωπίζουν την ακρίβεια, τους καθηλωμένους μισθούς, τα χιλιάδες κενά και τη διαρκή υποβάθμιση του δημόσιου σχολείου, η κυβέρνηση και το ΥΠΑΙΘΑ επιλέγουν να εντείνουν τις διώξεις και την καταστολή, αντί να δώσουν λύσεις στα πραγματικά προβλήματα της εκπαίδευσης. Το Δ.Σ. της ΟΛΜΕ απαιτεί: Να αθωωθούν οι συνάδελφοι Δ. Χαρτζουλάκη και Χ. Χοτζόγλου. Να απαλλαγούν από κάθε κατηγορία. Να σταματήσουν άμεσα όλες οι συνδικαλιστικές και πειθαρχικές διώξεις εκπαιδευτικών. Να ανακληθούν όλες οι πειθαρχικές παραπομπές που σχετίζονται με τη συμμετοχή στις συλλογικές αποφάσεις και κινητοποιήσεις του κλάδου. Να σταματήσει η ποινικοποίηση της συνδικαλιστικής δράσης και των αγώνων των εργαζομένων. Η ΟΛΜΕ στηρίζει την κινητοποίηση την Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου, στην Περιφερειακή Διεύθυνση Εκπαίδευσης Αττικής (Ξενίας 24, μετρό Μέγαρο Μουσικής), την ώρα εκδίκασης της πειθαρχικής υπόθεσης στις 9:30. Για τη διευκόλυνση των συναδέλφων/συναδεφισσών κηρύσσει 3ωρη παναττική στάση εργασίας 8:00 – 11:00 Καλούμε τις ΕΛΜΕ, τους εκπαιδευτικούς και όλα τα σωματεία να εκφράσουν έμπρακτα την αλληλεγγύη τους. Κάτω τα χέρια από τους συναδέλφους μας! Κάτω τα χέρια από τα σωματεία, την απεργία και τη συνδικαλιστική δράση! Η τρομοκρατία και οι διώξεις δεν θα περάσουν! www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Τρεις διαφορετικοί κόσμοι της σύγχρονης μουσικής συναντώνται στην Αθήνα το Σάββατο 20 Μαρτίου 2027, με τους Igorrr να ανεβαίνουν στη σκηνή του Gagarin 205, έχοντας στο πλευρό τους ως special guests τους Secret Chiefs 3 και τους Fange. Η ακραία μουσική χωρίς στεγανά βρίσκεται στο επίκεντρο μιας συναυλίας που φέρνει μαζί τρία ξεχωριστά ονόματα της experimental, avant-garde και extreme metal σκηνής. Οι Igorrr, οι Secret Chiefs 3 και οι Fange προσεγγίζουν τη μουσική από διαφορετικές αφετηρίες, συναντώνται όμως στην ίδια αναζήτηση: την υπέρβαση των καθιερωμένων ορίων και τη δημιουργία νέων ηχητικών κόσμων. Στο επίκεντρο βρίσκονται οι Igorrr, το προσωπικό μουσικό σύμπαν του Γάλλου συνθέτη, πολυοργανίστα και παραγωγού Gautier Serre. Από το 2005, όταν δημιούργησε το project, ο Serre εξερευνά τη συνύπαρξη φαινομενικά ασύμβατων μουσικών ειδών, συνδυάζοντας death και black metal με μπαρόκ αρμονίες, όπερα, breakcore, ηλεκτρονική παραγωγή και παραδοσιακές μουσικές. items.title: Αφού είδε ασθενείς να χάνουν την όρασή τους λόγω καθυστερήσεων, ο Surat Doctor παίρνει 30000 δωρεάν χειρουργικές επεμβάσεις σε χωριά
items.titleOriginal: After Seeing Patients Lose Sight To Delays, Surat Doctor Takes 30000 Free Surgeries to Villages
items.description: Από δωρεάν οφθαλμολογικό έλεγχο και γυαλιά μέχρι μεταφορά, χειρουργική επέμβαση, γεύματα και παρακολούθηση, η ομάδα του Dr Bhavin Patel βοηθά τις υποεξυπηρετούμενες κοινότητες σε όλο το Νότιο Γκουτζαράτ να έχουν πρόσβαση στην οφθαλμική φροντίδα.
items.descriptionOriginal: From free eye check-ups and glasses to transport, surgery, meals and follow-ups, Dr Bhavin Patel’s team helps underserved communities across South Gujarat access eye care.

items.descriptionOriginal: Στο λιμάνι της Θεσσαλονίκης αναμένεται να καταπλεύσει το πρωί της Παρασκευής, περίπου στις 08:00, η φρεγάτα « Κίμων ». Το κοινό θα έχει τη δυνατότητα να επισκεφθεί το πλοίο στο πλαίσιο των εκδηλώσεων για την επέτειο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου. Οι επισκέπτες θα μπορούν να περιηγηθούν στα εξωτερικά καταστρώματα με τη συνοδεία μελών του πληρώματος, που θα παρουσιάζουν τα συστήματα και τις δυνατότητες του πλοίου, σύμφωνα με το Πολεμικό Ναυτικό. Το πρόγραμμα επισκέψεων Σάββατο 24 Οκτωβρίου: 10:00-18:00 Κυριακή 25 Οκτωβρίου: 10:00-17:00 Δευτέρα 26 Οκτωβρίου: 10:00-12:00 για σχολεία και 12:00-17:00 για το κοινό Τρίτη 27 Οκτωβρίου: 10:00-12:00 για σχολεία και 12:00-17:00 για το κοινό Η είσοδος θα γίνεται μέσω των εγκαταστάσεων του Οργανισμού Λιμένος Θεσσαλονίκης. Στην αναλυτική λίστα του Πολεμικού Ναυτικού δεν αναφέρονται ώρες επισκεπτηρίου για την Τετάρτη 28 Οκτωβρίου, παρότι η ανακοίνωση αφορά συνολικά το διάστημα έως και εκείνη την ημέρα. www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Η Ουκρανία επιδιώκει να μεταφέρει τους τελωνειακούς ελέγχους των φορτηγών που μεταφέρουν σιτηρά και άλλα αγροτικά προϊόντα από τα σύνορα στο εσωτερικό γειτονικών χωρών της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, σε μια προσπάθεια να περιορίσει τον κίνδυνο ρωσικών επιθέσεων με μη επανδρωμένα αεροσκάφη, σύμφωνα με δημοσίευμα των Financial Times . Το Κίεβο βρίσκεται σε συνομιλίες με την Πολωνία και τη Σλοβακία για τη μεταφορά των ελέγχων στις επικράτειές τους, καθώς οι μεγάλες ουρές φορτηγών που περιμένουν να περάσουν τα σύνορα έχουν δεχθεί επανειλημμένα επιθέσεις από ρωσικά drones τις τελευταίες εβδομάδες. Η ουκρανική κυβέρνηση αναζητεί εναλλακτικές λύσεις για την ασφαλέστερη μεταφορά των εξαγωγών της, καθώς οι επιθέσεις της Μόσχας έχουν περιορίσει σημαντικά τη δυνατότητα χρήσης της παραδοσιακής θαλάσσιας οδού μέσω της Μαύρης Θάλασσας. Αρχείο – Reuters Συνομιλίες με Πολωνία και Σλοβακία Εκπρόσωπος του υπουργείου Εξωτερικών της Ουκρανίας, Γκεόργκι Τίχι, δήλωσε ότι το Κίεβο έχει ήδη δημιουργήσει κοινά σημεία συνοριακού ελέγχου με τη Μολδαβία και επιδιώκει να επεκτείνει το μοντέλο και σε άλλες γειτονικές χώρες, μεταξύ των οποίων η Πολωνία. Όπως εξήγησε, η πρωτοβουλία υπαγορεύεται από το νέο περιβάλλον ασφαλείας, στο οποίο η Ρωσία επιχειρεί, σύμφωνα με την ουκρανική πλευρά, να πλήξει τα σύνορα της χώρας, να διαταράξει τις μεταφορές και να εμποδίσει τη διακίνηση εμπορευμάτων. Το Κίεβο επιδιώκει να ολοκληρώσει τη συμφωνία με την Πολωνία το συντομότερο δυνατό. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή ανακοίνωσε ότι υποστηρίζει τις προσπάθειες για τη μεταφορά όλων των τελωνειακών ελέγχων στη μολδαβική πλευρά των συνόρων. Από τον Αύγουστο, η Ουκρανία έχει καταγράψει πολλαπλές επιθέσεις σε συνοριακά περάσματα με τη Ρουμανία, τη Μολδαβία και την Πολωνία. Οι επιθέσεις έχουν προκαλέσει μεγάλες ουρές φορτηγών και στις δύο πλευρές των συνόρων. Την Τετάρτη, η ουκρανική τελωνειακή υπηρεσία ανέφερε ότι περισσότερα από 1.200 φορτηγά περίμεναν να εισέλθουν στην Ουκρανία σε ένα μόνο συνοριακό πέρασμα στην περιφέρεια της Βολίν. Μείωση των εξαγωγών και απώλειες 60 εκατ. ευρώ ημερησίως Οι επιθέσεις στα μεγάλα ουκρανικά λιμάνια και στα πλοία που δραστηριοποιούνται στην περιοχή έχουν περιορίσει περίπου στο μισό τις εξαγωγές αγροτικών προϊόντων της χώρας, σύμφωνα με τον Ουκρανό υπουργό Γεωργίας, Ταράς Βισότσκι. Η Ουκρανία εξήγαγε τον Σεπτέμβριο 2,4 εκατομμύρια τόνους αγροτικών προϊόντων, ποσότητα που αντιστοιχεί μόλις στο 46% του δυνητικού όγκου των εξαγωγών της. «Χωρίς πλήρη πρόσβαση στα λιμάνια της Μαύρης Θάλασσας, αντιμετωπίζουμε ουσιαστικά ένα αντικειμενικό όριο στις εξαγωγές, στο 45% με 50%», ανέφερε ο Βισότσκι, υπογραμμίζοντας τη σημασία της διατήρησης και επέκτασης εναλλακτικών διαδρομών, σε συνεργασία με τους Ευρωπαίους εταίρους. Η επικεφαλής της ευρωπαϊκής διπλωματίας, Κάγια Κάλας, δήλωσε την Τετάρτη ότι η Ουκρανία χάνει περίπου 60 εκατομμύρια ευρώ ημερησίως σε έσοδα από εξαγωγές . Παράλληλα, το δημοσιονομικό κενό της χώρας για το επόμενο έτος εκτιμάται σε περίπου 70 δισ. ευρώ. Την περασμένη εβδομάδα, ο Γάλλος πρόεδρος Εμανουέλ Μακρόν τόνισε ότι η αποκατάσταση των εμπορικών διαδρομών της Ουκρανίας είναι απαραίτητη για τη χρηματοδότηση της οικονομίας και της πολεμικής της προσπάθειας, την ώρα που οι ευρωπαϊκές χώρες αντιμετωπίζουν αυξανόμενες πιέσεις για την παροχή οικονομικής στήριξης. Ο Μακρόν επισήμανε επίσης ότι οι ουκρανικές σοδειές βρίσκονται σε επίπεδα-ρεκόρ και συμβάλλουν στον εφοδιασμό πολλών αναπτυσσόμενων και φτωχών χωρών. Κατηγόρησε τη Ρωσία ότι, μέσω των επιθέσεών της, επιδιώκει να στερήσει τρόφιμα από αυτές τις χώρες και να αποδυναμώσει οικονομικά την Ουκρανία. Οι εναλλακτικές διαδρομές και τα προβλήματα στις μεταφορές Μετά τη ρωσική εισβολή τον Φεβρουάριο του 2022 και τον αποκλεισμό μεγάλου μέρους των ουκρανικών εξαγωγών από τη θάλασσα, η ΕΕ δημιούργησε τις λεγόμενες «λωρίδες αλληλεγγύης», ώστε τα ουκρανικά προϊόντα να μπορούν να μεταφέρονται μέσω ευρωπαϊκών χωρών. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή εντείνει τις προσπάθειες για την προώθηση των ουκρανικών αγροτικών προϊόντων προς την Αφρική και την Ασία. Παράλληλα, το Κίεβο έχει δηλώσει ότι εξετάζει τη χρήση λιμανιών στις χώρες της Βαλτικής για τη μεταφορά μέρους των εξαγωγών του, αν και το κόστος είναι σημαντικά υψηλότερο σε σύγκριση με τη διαδρομή μέσω της Μαύρης Θάλασσας. Σύμφωνα με την Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή, ο όγκος των ουκρανικών εμπορευμάτων που μεταφέρθηκαν μέσω του Δούναβη σχεδόν διπλασιάστηκε, από περίπου 600.000 τόνους τον Αύγουστο σε 1,16 εκατομμύρια τόνους τον Σεπτέμβριο. Τον ίδιο μήνα, μόλις το 10% των ουκρανικών εξαγωγών διακινήθηκε μέσω της Μαύρης Θάλασσας. Ωστόσο, οι εναλλακτικές διαδρομές αντιμετωπίζουν σημαντικά εμπόδια. Τα σιδηροδρομικά δίκτυα και τα κανάλια είναι υπερφορτωμένα, ενώ η χαμηλή στάθμη του Δούναβη, έπειτα από την καλοκαιρινή ξηρασία, έχει περιορίσει τις δυνατότητες μεταφοράς φορτίων. Την ίδια στιγμή, η Πολωνία, η Ουγγαρία και η Σλοβακία έχουν απαγορεύσει τις εισαγωγές ουκρανικών σιτηρών, επιτρέποντας ωστόσο τη διέλευσή τους υπό περιορισμούς προς άλλες χώρες. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή υπογραμμίζει ότι η ανάπτυξη εναλλακτικών διαδρομών μεταφοράς παραμένει βασική προτεραιότητα, λόγω των συνεχιζόμενων ρωσικών επιθέσεων στα ουκρανικά λιμάνια, στις μεταφορικές υποδομές και στα συνοριακά περάσματα. Παράλληλα, αναζητείται εξοπλισμός και τροχαίο υλικό για την ενίσχυση του ουκρανικού σιδηροδρομικού δικτύου. www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Organic molecules have produced an electronic behavior that researchers have struggled to engineer in molecular materials. Scientists assembled triptycene-based molecules into a rare two-dimensional lattice and detected quantum states confined to its edges. The finding could widen the options for designing materials used in future electronic and quantum devices. The structure combines features of honeycomb and Kagome lattices, arrangements that scientists study for their unusual electronic properties. Its edge states also demonstrate that organic molecular assemblies can support topological behavior, an area of research dominated by inorganic materials. The findings appeared in Nano Letters on Sept. 2, 2026. The international team included researchers from Japan’s National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), several Japanese universities, and Germany’s Kiel University. Hybrid molecular lattice The researchers created what scientists call a diatomic Kagome lattice. Its geometry combines elements of two distinct lattice patterns. Honeycomb lattices resemble a beehive’s repeating cells. Graphene, a single layer of graphite, follows this arrangement. Kagome lattices take their name from a traditional Japanese basket-weaving pattern. Scientists have extensively investigated both structures because their geometry can produce distinctive electronic properties. However, researchers have rarely fabricated a diatomic Kagome lattice in an actual material. The team used derivatives of triptycene, a molecule whose three planes form a propeller-like arrangement. Those molecular planes make contact with neighboring structures, strengthening electronic interactions within the assembled material. That detail matters because organic molecules typically couple weakly through electronic interactions. Their structures offer considerable design flexibility, but those weak connections can make it difficult to reproduce the properties required for quantum materials. Unusual states at edges The team examined its molecular assembly using a scanning tunneling microscope. The measurements revealed electronic states concentrated along the structure’s boundary, where the lattice meets its surroundings. The researchers then used theoretical analysis to identify these features as topological edge states. These states emerge from the topology, or mathematical structure, of a material’s electronic properties. They occupy the edges rather than behaving like electronic states within the interior. Their presence provides evidence that the organic assembly exhibits the distinctive properties of a topological quantum material. The strong electronic coupling between neighboring triptycene derivatives helps explain how the structure supports this behavior. The result offers researchers a different way to approach quantum material design. Instead of relying primarily on inorganic compounds, scientists can investigate how molecular geometry and stronger electronic interactions create useful quantum properties. Future quantum applications The team sees potential applications in electronics that consume less power and switch states rapidly. Future studies could investigate whether related structures can transition between semiconductor-like behavior and superconductivity. Researchers also envision ultra-fast optical switches and energy transport without losses at room temperature. Neither capability has been demonstrated in this experiment, and achieving them would require further research. The immediate achievement is more specific. Scientists have shown that an organic molecular assembly can host topologica l edge states through a deliberately engineered lattice. That gives researchers a new structure to investigate as they work to understand how molecular design can control electronic behavior.

items.title: «Το δάσος είναι το σπίτι μου»: Αντιμετώπισε τη βροχή, τις βδέλλες και τις σκοτεινές νύχτες για να ελέγξει 3000+ βατράχους για μια θανατηφόρα ασθένεια
items.titleOriginal: ‘The Forest Is My Home’: She Braved Rain, Leeches & Dark Nights To Check 3000+ Frogs for a Deadly Disease
items.description: Κάθε φορά που η μητέρα της Keerthi Krutha, T V Champakalatha, της ζητούσε να γυρίσει σπίτι για φεστιβάλ, συχνά λάμβανε μια απάντηση που έλεγε τα πάντα για την αγάπη της κόρης της για την ερημιά. items.descriptionOriginal: Whenever Keerthi Krutha's mother, T V Champakalatha, asked her to come home for festivals, she often received an answer that said everything about her daughter's love for the wilderness. "Amma, I am already home. The forest is my home," Keerthi would tell her. For the 36-year-old Chennai-born wildlife researcher, the forests of the Western Ghats had become part of everyday life. After sunset, when frogs began calling from streams and insects filled the air with their sounds, she would set out with a torch, sampling kits and notebooks. Her task was to find the frogs, collect samples from their skin, record what she saw and release them unharmed. Some nights meant crossing slippery rocks and swollen streams. Others brought leeches, unpredictable rain and hours of walking. Yet these were the places Keerthi had always wanted to be. Over several years, working largely on her own, she surveyed 49 protected areas and 19 other landscapes , documenting more than 3,000 amphibians. She was searching for answers to a worrying question: was a fungus that had devastated frogs in other parts of the world spreading through India's forests too? Her research would help scientists understand where the fungus had reached in the Western Ghats and how to keep checking for it. "If frogs are dying, then it means there is a problem," Keerthi told The Hindu in 2015. "Frogs are ecological indicators." Speaking to The Better India , she traces this work back to a childhood spent learning about snakes, crocodiles and forests. It began with a childhood love for wildlife Growing up in Chennai, Keerthi looked forward to nature documentaries and filled her shelves with wildlife books. Family trips often took her to forests rather than popular tourist attractions. The more she learnt, the more time she wanted outdoors. "It wasn't something that came suddenly," her mother tells The Better India . "Nature was always where she felt happiest." Growing up in Chennai, Keerthi looked forward to nature documentaries and filled her shelves with wildlife books. In 2004, as a school student, Keerthi was selected as a Sanctuary Asia Tiger Ambassador through the Kids for Tigers programme. Visits to protected forests introduced her to people who had made wildlife conservation their life's work. Conservation began to feel like a possible future. She also volunteered at the Madras Crocodile Bank, helping clean crocodile enclosures after the 2004 tsunami. While studying for a BTech in Biotechnology at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University in Coimbatore, she joined local snake rescues, participated in wildlife estimation exercises and volunteered with conservation organisations. "Wildlife became the direction she wanted her life to take," her mother says. By the time Keerthi graduated in 2012, she knew she wanted to work in conservation. An opportunity soon took her back into the forests, this time to study frogs. Looking for a fungus in frogs After graduating, she joined a project run by the Wildlife Information Liaison Development (WILD) Society and Zoo Outreach Organisation, affiliated with the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Pune. The team was investigating a fungus that infects frogs and other amphibians in the Western Ghats. It causes a disease called chytridiomycosis . Scientists call the fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis , or simply chytrid fungus. The fungus attacks their skin, which frogs rely on to absorb water and breathe. In some frogs, a serious infection can be fatal. "It has resulted in the extinction of nearly 200 species of frogs globally and threatens almost 40 percent of amphibian species," Keerthi tells The Better India . The Western Ghats, one of the world's biodiversity hotspots, are home to more than 200 frog species, many found nowhere else. Although India had not seen the mass frog deaths reported elsewhere, scientists had already detected the fungus in several species. "The incidence of this disease was recorded for the first time here in 2011," Keerthi explains. "That made long-term monitoring especially important." Researchers needed to find out which forests harboured the fungus and whether it appeared in new places over time. That meant searching for frogs in the wild, without hurting them. Keerthi was ready to do the work. What it takes to survey thousands of frogs after dark Frogs are especially active at night. Following their calls, Keerthi searched rainforests, evergreen forests, shola grasslands and streams, often working until late in the nights. Even finding these tiny animals could take hours. She carefully took a skin swab from each frog, recorded its details and released it. The swabs could then be tested for fungus without harming the animals. On one of her expeditions, her mother joined her and saw how difficult and demanding her work really was. Between surveys, she stayed in forest camps. Leeches, slippery paths, rising streams and unpredictable weather became familiar parts of the work. On one visit, her mother joined her and saw what these nights demanded. "I realised how difficult and demanding the work really was," she tells The Better India . "But I also knew she was exactly where she wanted to be." For Keerthi, each sample brought scientists closer to understanding the possible danger facing the animals she had spent so long searching for. How tiny skin samples helped track a hidden threat Collecting frogs' skin samples was only half the job. Scientists also needed a reliable way to repeat these checks in different forests and compare what they found. Keerthi helped develop clear steps for finding frogs, taking samples and recording results, so other researchers could follow the same process in the years ahead. Tests at IISER Pune found that the fungus belonged to a type already known to occur widely in Asia. The findings were published in the scientific journal PLOS ONE , adding to what researchers knew about its presence in the Western Ghats. As the work expanded, Keerthi independently secured two grants from the Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund. This allowed the surveys to reach more places and the team to continue documenting frogs. The samples and methods gave future researchers a starting point for checking whether the disease was spreading or changing over time. An unexpected discovery in the woods The forests held another surprise. While studying a disease already known to scientists, Keerthi and her colleagues helped identify a frog species that had never been formally described. In 2017, they described Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi , or Mewa Singh's night frog, found only in Kerala's Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary. Discoveries like this help scientists understand where a species lives and which habitats may need protection. But finding a species is only the first step. Understanding the threats it faces is equally important, and frogs themselves can offer valuable clues. Tigers and elephants often draw the spotlight in wildlife conservation. Frogs are easier to overlook, but they can tell us a great deal about the health of our forests. Their skin absorbs water and helps them breathe, making them especially sensitive to pollution, habitat damage and disease. When frog populations begin to decline, it can be an early warning that something is wrong in their surroundings, potentially affecting other wildlife too. "If frogs are dying, then it means there is a problem," Keerthi says. This is what makes her research so important. By identifying where the fungus has been found, Keerthi is helping scientists keep watch for a threat that could affect frogs across the Western Ghats, including species found nowhere else on Earth. For Keerthi, the forest has always been home The child who explored tiger reserves , cleaned crocodile enclosures after the tsunami and rescued snakes grew into a researcher documenting frogs and helping scientists understand a disease threatening them worldwide. Her surveys, scientific work and role in discovering a new species have added to what we know about the Western Ghats and the wildlife that depends on them. Her mother has watched that commitment carry Keerthi through long field trips and festivals away from home. "She has always chosen the forest," she says. All Pictures: Keerthikrutha Seetharaman

items.descriptionOriginal: General Motors (GM) says it virtually tested more than 300,000 electric vehicle battery designs before building a physical prototype, helping the US automaker move from its first battery-pack concept to formal program approval in just one month. The achievement is part of GM’s development of its fourth-generation EV platform, which aims to deliver longer driving ranges, lower manufacturing costs and simpler vehicle designs. The company is using computer simulations and a new engineering approach that allows design, manufacturing and engineering teams to work simultaneously rather than completing their tasks one after another. GM expects the approach to cut its traditional five-year vehicle development timeline in half. Testing 300,000 battery designs At the center of the new platform is lithium manganese-rich (LMR) battery technology, which GM is developing for its high-volume electric vehicles. Instead of manufacturing and physically testing hundreds of battery designs, engineers used computer models to evaluate more than 300,000 possible configurations before producing a prototype. According to GM, this helped its engineering team move from an initial LMR battery-pack concept to formal program approval in just one month. The batteries will use prismatic cells manufactured by Ultium Cells, GM’s joint venture with LG Energy Solution, in Spring Hill, Tennessee. GM says its LMR chemistry is designed to deliver 33% greater energy density than lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, a widely used lower-cost alternative. Higher energy density could allow automakers to achieve longer driving ranges without increasing battery size or weight. GM estimates that its fourth-generation EV platform, combining LMR batteries with improved electric motors and aerodynamics, could deliver roughly 20% more driving range per kilowatt-hour of energy than its current vehicles. These improvements remain targets for the upcoming platform rather than independently verified performance figures. Simplifying future electric vehicles Beyond batteries, GM is redesigning the motors, electronics and electrical systems used in its next generation of EVs. The company says its new electric drive units contain 40% fewer parts, making them smaller and lighter while potentially reducing manufacturing costs. Its updated electrical architecture also uses 30% less wiring and fewer control modules than current GM electric vehicles. A centralized computing system is designed to provide 40 times more processing power, supporting software updates, energy management, and driver-assistance features such as Super Cruise. GM is also extending digital simulations into vehicle manufacturing . Engineers can use virtual models to examine assembly procedures, equipment placement and potential safety issues before installing production machinery. Once manufacturing begins, GM’s PlantBrAIn system will combine factory-floor information with computer models to identify ways to improve production. The automaker says similar methods have already helped its battery-pack assembly facilities process battery packs 30% faster. Future vehicles will also be able to check their electrical connections during assembly, potentially eliminating a final electrical validation step. GM has not specified when its fourth-generation EV platform will enter production. The company says the changes are intended to make electric vehicles more affordable while accelerating development and manufacturing.

items.description: Μια γυναίκα που πετούσε United από το Χάντσβιλ στο Χιούστον το απόγευμα της Τετάρτης του Ιουνίου επιβιβάστηκε στο περιφερειακό τζετ και διαπίστωσε ότι το είχε για τον εαυτό της. Κάτω από το όνομα χρήστη u/Sufficient_Fudge_280 , αργότερα δημοσίευσε μια φωτογραφία του άδειου αεροπλάνου στο Reddit με λεζάντα, «Κατά κάποιο τρόπο το μόνο άτομο στην πτήση μου και ο πιλότος ήταν τόσο ανόητος χαζός». Κάπως το μόνο άτομο…
items.descriptionOriginal: A woman flying United from Huntsville to Houston on a Wednesday evening in June boarded the regional jet and found she had it to herself . Under the username u/Sufficient_Fudge_280 , she later posted a photo of the empty plane on Reddit captioned, “Somehow the only person on my flight and the pilot was such a goofy goober.” Somehow the only person on my flight and the pilot was such a goofy goober by u/Sufficient_Fudge_280 in unitedairlines She got her own personalized preflight announcements . The flight attendant also ran the full safety demonstration for an audience of one, laughing the whole way through it. Before takeoff, the crew brought sandbags into the cabin. She wrote that it was “bc the plane was too light with only one passenger,” though that isn’t quite the reason. It’s not that planes are too light to fly, but with an empty cabin, the center of gravity can shift, and that extra weight pulls it back in. On a small regional jet with one person aboard, sandbags are a normal way to solve that problem. A woman walks down the aisle of an empty flight. Photo credit: Yosuke Ota via Unsplash . After landing and taxiing in, the captain invited her up to the flight deck to sit in the seat and look around. “The crew was so cool,” she wrote, adding that the whole thing was funny and joyful. Reddit mostly enjoyed it, with one commenter calling it a “poor man’s private jet.” Another said, “I would have been freaking out at the gate, thinking I was in the wrong place because nobody else was there.” A third quipped, “Still made her gate check her bag for lack of bin space.” The post A woman boarded a United flight and realized she was the only passenger. Then the pilot made it unforgettable. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: Rookie NFL receiver was mocked for his stutter. Now he speaks to the media every single week.
items.description: Ο KC Concepcion ήταν ένας σούπερ σταρ ευρείας δέκτης στην Texas A&M και πολύ γνωστός στους θαυμαστές του College Station. Αλλά όταν μπήκε στο NFL Draft αυτή την περασμένη offseason, παρουσιάστηκε σε ένα εντελώς νέο κοινό που δεν ήταν εξοικειωμένο μαζί του. Σε μια σχεδόν 15λεπτη εμφάνιση στα μέσα μαζικής ενημέρωσης στο συγκρότημα NFL τον Φεβρουάριο του 2026, στέκοντας σόλο στο βάθρο…
items.descriptionOriginal: KC Concepcion was a superstar wide receiver at Texas A&M and well known to the College Station fanbase. But when he entered the NFL Draft this past offseason, he introduced himself to an entirely new audience that was mostly unfamiliar with him. In a nearly 15-minute media appearance at the NFL combine in February 2026, standing solo at the podium fielding questions from NFL reporters, Concepcion’s lifelong stutter was on full display. KC Concepcion has battled ridicule his whole life over stutter In an open letter penned in The Players’ Tribune earlier this year, Concepcion opened up about his struggles growing up with a speech impediment. You’d think being a rising star football player would make anyone immune to bullying, but apparently not when you have a severe stutter. It’s a condition that’s almost impossible to hide in daily life. “The other kids at school, they’d notice how I’d get stuck on certain words. Or that it would take me a second to respond to the teacher, or to tell them my name,” he wrote. “They’d point at me, or make faces, or raise their eyebrows, and then it’d be like…. ‘What’s wrong with you?!??!’ Or ‘Why can’t you talk normal? Are you dumb or something????’ Dead in my face. While cracking up laughing. Not with me , or even about me…. At me. Man … it was tough.” He also writes about how his stutter would disappear “like magic” when he was away from school and not being teased. But in front of his peers, it would always return. Stress and anxiety have been shown to make stuttering noticeably worse. “And back then, how I would deal with my situation is, a lot of times … I’d basically just not talk,” he writes. Star receiver’s stutter remains to this day KC Concepcion still struggles with his speech, though speech classes as a kid helped. His stutter never fully went away. Looking back on his childhood, Concepcion admits that “kids are mean sometimes.” But when he fielded questions from reporters at the NFL Combine in February, he once again faced ridicule from trolls and online bullies. He was in line for a life-changing career move and payday, but instead of soaking up the moment, he felt like he was back on the playground. But this time, he had the perfect response ready. Per Sports Illustrated , Concepcion wrote on his Instagram: “I just wanna say something, if you have a speech impediment, there is nothing wrong with us. I have had this stutter since I can remember talking this is apart of me this is who I am I cannot control this. I wanna be a role model for those who may be scared to speak.” View this post on Instagram Concepcion follows through on his role model promise in the NFL Today, Concepcion is enjoying a solid start to his NFL career as a wide receiver for the Cleveland Browns. But it’s what he’s doing off the field that’s having an even bigger impact. All NFL players are required to speak to the media and perform certain public relations obligations. But Concepcion goes one step further. Despite his speech issues, he doesn’t shy away from the camera and makes a point of speaking on camera every week. At times, the words flow freely out of him. Other times, he struggles with his stutter. But he refuses to fade into the background or hide from the camera. It makes a huge difference for people with speech impediments all over the world. “I wish I had someone like you to represent us stutterers back then. I remember being picked on by adults … for having a stutter and it irked me! I was only a kid, and I still stutter to this day. I’ve always felt insecure about it and I always envy those who can speak fluently,” one commenter wrote on Concepcion’s Instagram. “I learned later on the line that there’s no such thing as perfect speech and having a stutter is ok. Always embrace what you have and don’t let the negative feedback stop you from grinding. You’re a real one.” “You are changing the world on and off the field! As a speech-language pathologist who works exclusively with people who stutter, I see every day how powerful it is when someone speaks openly and unapologetically!” said another. “KC I don’t know you, however I’m very proud of you and what you’ve accomplished. For NOT letting a speech impediment define you. Taking risks and accomplishments that do not go unnoticed,” someone added. “My 12 year old son, who also stutters and has since age 3, had the PRIVILEGE of meeting KC [before a game]. It was an awesome and inspiring moment that my son definitely will never forgot and it TRULY inspired us all!! He told my son, ‘You and me, we’re the same. We go through the same things everyday. But don’t ever let nobody tell you what you cannot do. Be great my boy,'” shared another. It takes tremendous courage and confidence to speak in front of dozens of reporters, with cameras rolling and untold numbers of fans watching at home. But Concepcion finds strength in paving the way for others like him. “So, to any kid out there who is carrying something heavy right now — a stutter, something that makes you feel different, anything that’s ever made someone look at you sideways,” he wrote in his open letter. “Just know this: My success … it is your success , too.” The post Rookie NFL receiver was mocked for his stutter. Now he speaks to the media every single week. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Όταν ένα πρώτο ραντεβού πάει καλά, μπορείτε να το πείτε. Μπορεί να είναι τόσο προφανές όσο ένα συναινετικό φιλί για καληνύχτα ή τόσο διακριτικό όσο μια κλεμμένη ματιά πάνω από το επιδόρπιο. Έπειτα, υπάρχουν τα λιγότερο προφανή λόγια, όπως οι ανεπαίσθητες κινήσεις του σώματος που κάνουμε όταν αισθανόμαστε έλξη προς ένα πιθανό ερωτικό ταίρι, και ο ήχος της φωνής μας. Είτε νιώθουμε σύνδεση κατά τη διάρκεια ενός ραντεβού i…
items.descriptionOriginal: When a first date goes well , you can tell. It can be as obvious as a consensual goodnight kiss or as subtle as a stolen glance over dessert. Then there are the less obvious tells, like the imperceptible body movements we make when we feel drawn towards a potential love match, and the sound of our voice. Whether we feel a connection during a date isn’t just about what we see, but also what we hear . According to a new study , our vocal cords can reveal our true romantic intentions before we even realize it. These subtle shifts in our voices can show whether we feel a spark with someone or feel compelled to pursue a longer-term relationship. How men and women unconsciously signal interest The study focused on a speed-dating session with 30 single adults, ages 20 to 40 . Afterward, each person reported back on who they wanted to see again. The researchers then examined all the conversations and analyzed each person’s voice. They looked at average pitch, lowest pitch, and pitch variability. The spontaneous shifts in these categories showed a clear pattern. When male participants talked to women they wanted to see again, they lowered their average pitch. This shift became even stronger when the attraction was completely mutual. Men’s vocal timbre also dropped the lowest around women who were popular with other suitors. Women’s voices did something entirely different and surprisingly complex. With men they liked, their voices rose and became more varied. With the men most in demand among other women, their tone dipped lower, but only when they also liked those men personally. Men, in turn, preferred women with lower-pitched voices. A woman’s lowest pitch accounted for up to 55% of the differences in men’s preferences. Overall, subtle acoustic adjustments reveal who we want to impress. The evolutionary reason behind our vocal shifts These vocal changes are not accidental. They are evolutionary tools hardwired into our biology. Women tend to modulate their pitch to better match their social setting. The pitch they use at work likely differs from the one they use with friends or on a first date. For men, dropping their pitch signals capability and strength. Lower voices, regardless of gender, naturally convey confidence, status, and physical presence. A bigger Penn State study backs this up. Researchers had more than 3,100 people in 22 countries listen to the same sentence at different pitches. When asked, both men and women preferred lower voices for a long-term partner. It makes sense that when you’re first meeting someone, you’re looking for quick insights, and how they speak is a fast clue. Context matters, though. Respondents noted that higher-pitched female voices sounded more flirtatious. Men in the survey stated that this vocal variation made these women more attractive to them for short-term relationships. Next time you’re on a date, remember to listen closely to more than just the other person’s words. Pay attention to their voice. Oh, and ask follow-up questions. People like that. The post Researchers discovered a secret vocal signal that reveals when someone is attracted to you appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Ο David Bowie και ο Bing Crosby ήταν πάντα λίγο απίθανο ζευγάρι. Κι όμως, απέδειξαν ότι όταν δύο απίστευτα ταλέντα ενώνουν τις δυνάμεις τους, μπορεί να συμβεί μια βουτιά μαγείας. Η ιστορία τους δείχνει επίσης ότι συχνά χρειάζεται ένα χωριό για να λειτουργήσει ένα τραγούδι, και αυτό ακριβώς συνέβη με το απίστευτα δημοφιλές χριστουγεννιάτικο ντουέτο τους. Ήταν Σεπτέμβριος του 1977 και η…
items.descriptionOriginal: David Bowie and Bing Crosby were always a bit of an unlikely pair. And yet, they proved that when two incredible talents join forces, a splash of magic can happen. Their story also illustrates that it often takes a village to make a song work, and that was exactly the case with their incredibly popular Christmas duet. It was September 1977, and the air in England was just beginning to turn crisp. American crooner Crosby was recording his Christmas special and had agreed to have David Bowie accompany him on the classic “Little Drummer Boy.” But there was a tiny ripple in the plan. ‘A fascinating combination’ In a behind-the-scenes interview posted on PBS, songwriter and composer Alan “Buz” Kohan (who had also written for Michael Jackson and many other artists) shared what went down when Bowie first heard the arrangement. First, Kohan explained that the production company Smith-Hemion thought Bowie and Crosby were a perfect match. They “figured it would be a fascinating combination, since we were shooting in England anyway, to see if we can get some genuine English performers to appear on the show. And we got Twiggy, and we got some other English artists that were basically only known in England; they didn’t actually translate to America.” Bowie’s answer surprised Kohan. “I don’t know why Bowie said yes, but he did because he was Ziggy Stardust at the time, which is about as far away from Bing Crosby as you could get.” Bowie wasn’t feeling it Only there was a bit of a problem. Kohan continued, “We were going to shoot what was ostensibly just ‘Little Drummer Boy.’ And when we got into rehearsal with him, he said, ‘I don’t really like that song.’ Well, OK, I seem to remember that he said, ‘It doesn’t show off my range now.’ I don’t know if that’s why he didn’t like it or he was just not enamored of it. But anyway, we had this arrangement written out and everything, and the track was made, and everything was set.” He and the writing and music team knew they had a job to do and they had to do it quickly. Kohan shared that he told Bowie, “‘Well, let’s just see what we can do to make it palatable for you,’ and Larry Grossman (composer) and I and Ian Fraser, who was the music director, went down to a little room with a piano. And we decided the best way to salvage the arrangement was to do a counter melody that would fit in between the spaces. And maybe write a new bridge and see if we can sell them that.” ‘Peace on Earth’ was born That is exactly what they did in just about an hour. Kohan continued, “It all happened rather rapidly. I would say within an hour we had it written, and we’re able to present it to him again…We played it for him; he says, ‘Yeah, I like that. I can do that. I think that’s good.’ So he spent about that much time rehearsing it with Bing, and we shot it that day. And that was basically how ‘Peace on Earth’ and ‘Little Drummer Boy’ got married, and we had no trouble picking that up that quickly.” Kohan then explained how rapidly Crosby was able to pick up new material. “He was, in addition to being very articulate, a very bright and aware person. He always knew what was going on around him and he always was able to transform himself without losing any of the Crosby-isms, that relaxed that feeling and the atmosphere that he would always create whenever he was on camera. But he used to love to learn new material.” The collaboration has become one of the most beloved holiday tunes of all time. Though the opening spoken intro might feel a bit forced, the music makes it all worth it. Crosby’s warm baritone traditional parts lie like velvet underneath Bowie’s soul-piercing higher register. It was two voices, two songs, two generations, marinating together like high-end ingredients making the finest meal. Two generations collide Billboard shared a 2014 AP article relaying that Bing’s daughter Mary had thoughts right away. Speaking to a summer TV critics tour, she said: “The doors opened and David walked in with his wife. They were both wearing full-length mink coats, they had matching full makeup, and their hair was bright red…We were thinking, ‘Oh my god.’” Bing’s son Nathaniel added, “It almost didn’t happen. I think the producers told him to take the lipstick off and take the earring out. It was just incredible to see the contrast.” The Christmas special Merrie Olde Christmas was released at the end of November that year. Nearly five years later, RCA released the song as a single. It is still played on radio stations around the world today. A ‘quirky’ idea For his part, Bowie was candid about how strange the combination was. In a 1990 promotional interview , he shared, “The idea I thought was so quirky, it was worth doing. I thought it was an extraordinary situation to be in. And I knew that nobody else would probably do that kind of thing. They don’t, do they?” The post David Bowie disliked Bing Crosby’s duet choice. A last-minute rewrite became a Christmas classic. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Είναι κολίβριο, γεράκι ή σκόρος; Το κάπως συγκεχυμένο όνομα κολιμπρί είναι (drumroll, παρακαλώ) ένα είδος σκώρου που μεταναστεύει στο Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο και την Ιρλανδία από τη Νότια Ευρώπη και τη Βόρεια Αφρική κάθε καλοκαίρι. Το όνομά του προέρχεται από τον τρόπο που τρέφεται - αιωρείται πάνω από λουλούδια σαν κολίβριο. Ο φωτογράφος άγριας ζωής Andrew Fusek-Peters φωτογραφήθηκε…
items.descriptionOriginal: Is it a hummingbird, a hawk, or a moth? The somewhat confusingly named hummingbird hawk-moth is (drumroll, please) a moth species that migrates to the U.K. and Ireland from southern Europe and North Africa each summer. Its moniker comes from the way it feeds — hovering over flowers like a hummingbird. Wildlife photographer Andrew Fusek-Peters captured that feeding process earlier this month in a series of stunning photos that show the 2-inch insect beating its wings at a staggering 85 times a second while drinking from a valerian bush in his garden in Shropshire, England. Andrew Fusek-Peters / SWNS The striking moths have been thriving in the U.K. thanks to the warm summer. James Benwell, from the Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust, told the BBC that 2026 was a “record year” for sightings in the country. “They’ve had a really good year this year,” he said. “Normally they would come in small numbers. We’d normally hear of a few maybe. But this year, we’ve seen loads of records of them.” Andrew Fusek-Peters / SWNS Though it borrows its name from the hummingbird, this hawk-moth actually has the avian species beat when it comes to hovering speed — hummingbirds average about 50 beats per second, while the insects can hit up to 85 beats per second. (Another fun fact: Hummingbirds are native only to the Americas, and hummingbird hawk-moths only to the U.K., Europe, and North Africa.) “The hummingbird hawk-moth is a summer visitor to the U.K. from southern Europe and North Africa but can be seen in most months of the year and is a favorite garden visitor,” Fusek-Peters told SWNS. “With warmer summers, it now breeds in the U.K. and will often overwinter here and can now be considered a U.K. breeding species.” He noted that the bugs “emit an audible hum” as they hover. “It means that it can maneuver easily with its long proboscis able to delve into deeper flower stems such as red valerian.” Andrew Fusek-Peters / SWNS As for how he captured such action-packed photos, Fusek-Peters said it took time and experimentation. “I spent much of the summer photographing them and experimented with slowing down my shutter speed to capture the incredible motion and orange flash of the wings.” This article was originally written by Ed Chatterton for SWNS — the U.K.’s largest independent news agency, providing globally relevant original, verified, and engaging content to the world’s leading media outlets.

items.descriptionOriginal: Researchers at the the University of Surrey have developed a library of 28 materials to help identify better candidates for building sodium-ion batteries. ​The repository could help find alternative materials to replace the conventional lithium-ion batteries that are made from scarce resources. ​”We rely heavily on lithium-ion batteries, but lithium resources are relatively scarce and unevenly distributed around the world,” said Daniel Commandeur, lecturer at the School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering and corresponding author of the study. ​He noted that sodium-ion batteries are emerging as a robust alternative; however, it need further analysis to improve their performance over repeated charging cycles and the amount of energy they can hold. ​”Sodium is far more abundant, making sodium-ion batteries an important technology to develop,” Commandeur added. ​Library to access performance The team explored how modifying the chemical composition of sodium manganese oxide could improve its performance as a cathode. This key battery component determines how much energy a battery can store and how efficiently it operates. During the investigation, they created a library composed of 28 different metal compositions and compared their performance in sodium-ion batteries . The collection was made by replacing the manganese with varying amounts of different metals, including iron, titanium, and vanadium. ​Iron boosted energy-storage capacity, vanadium improved cycling stability, and small amounts of titanium enhanced high-rate performance. Some titanium-containing materials retained over 90% of their capacity after 100 charge-discharge cycles , the study found. ​AI to pace the hunt The team agreed that a major hurdle is finding a material that delivers the optimum performance. ​To help explore suitable alternative materials, researchers developed an automated approach to analyze the data generated by the experiments. They trained the machine-learning models with datasets generated in their experiments. ​”This work is a first step toward building the larger data sets needed for machine learning to guide that search—helping us identify promising materials faster and accelerate the development of better sodium-ion batteries,” said Commandeur. ​Researchers said expanding the dataset could eventually let AI predict promising battery compositions before they are produced and tested in the lab. However, the current library remains too small for reliable predictions. ​Expanding the approach to a wider range of cathode materials could generate the large, high-quality datasets needed for machine learning to accelerate the discovery of new battery materials. In time, this could help scientists design sodium-ion cathodes optimized for specific needs, such as higher energy storage, faster charging , or longer-lasting performance. “What stood out most was how relatively small changes in composition could shift the balance between how much energy a material can store, how it performs at higher rates, and how well it lasts. Mapping those relationships gives us a much clearer picture of where to look next,” said Eden Marks, a Ph.D. student in space engineering and co-lead author of the study. ​The findings were published in a new study in the Journal of Materials Chemistry .

items.descriptionOriginal: When some people wake up in the morning , the first thing they do is try to make sense of what happened in their dreams. Whether it was a terrifying night terror where they were pursued by a shadowy figure, or a delightful trip back in time to when they were a child , dreams can affect how we start the day. But for others, they wake up to their alarm and go about their day without even thinking about what happened during the night. It’s as if their brains were wiped clean when they woke up and they never had a dream at all. A 2021 CBS News poll found that 11% of people always remember their dreams, 10% never recall a thing, and the other 79% fall somewhere in between. Why do some people remember their dreams and others do not? A dreamlike state. Photo credit: Canva According to research, people who can remember their dreams have higher activity in their temporoparietal junction , an area of the brain involved in understanding others’ thoughts, shifting attention, and taking different perspectives. “There’s a region in your brain called the temporoparietal junction , which processes information and emotions. This region can also put you in a state of intra-sleep wakefulness, which, in turn, allows your brain to encode and remember dreams better,” Julie Lambert, certified sleep expert, told Healthline in a medically reviewed article . “Researchers also looked at the most common personality traits that are presented in people who can recall their dreams,” Lambert continued. “Overall, such people are prone to daydreaming, creative thinking, and introspection. At the same time, those who are more practical and focused on what is outside themselves tend to have difficulty remembering their dreams.” A young girl having a nightmare. Photo credit: Canva How are people who recall their dreams different? So, if you always recall your dreams, chances are that you are more creative, introspective, and prone to daydreaming. That’s because the temporoparietal junction is associated with the ability to understand other people’s mental states. It also allows us to shift our perspectives from one person or topic to another and pay attention to sudden changes in the environment. This ability to see things from multiple perspectives, easily engage with the world outside ourselves, and shift mindsets is a hallmark of creative thinking. A person with such abilities is more likely to daydream while out on a walk. The problem with people who always remember their dreams While interesting, remembering our dreams has a downside. People who show high activity in the temporoparietal junction may have difficulty sleeping. When that area of the brain is active, it means it’s harder to ignore outside stimuli, which makes it harder to remain in a deep sleep. If you wake up every morning still feeling the emotions of the vivid dreams you’ve had, that shows you are deeply connected to the part of your brain that’s creative and empathetic. Let’s hope those amazing character traits are a decent trade-off for being a little groggy in the morning. This article originally appeared in June. It has been updated. The post People who always remember their dreams don’t sleep as well, but have three impressive qualities appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Μια μαθήτρια δημιούργησε κατά λάθος μια επαναφορτιζόμενη μπαταρία που θα μπορούσε να κρατήσει 400 χρόνια

items.description: Ένα απόσπασμα που αποδίδεται ευρέως στον Ρωμαίο φιλόσοφο Σενέκα λέει: «Η τύχη συμβαίνει όταν η προετοιμασία συναντά την ευκαιρία». Το 2016, ένας υποψήφιος διδάκτορας στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Καλιφόρνια Irvine απέδειξε ότι αυτή είναι όντως η αλήθεια. Πριν από δέκα χρόνια, η Mya Le Thai, PhD έπαιζε στο εργαστήριο όταν έκανε μια κολοσσιαία ανακάλυψη που θα μπορούσε να οδηγήσει σε επαναφόρτιση…
items.descriptionOriginal: A quote widely attributed to the Roman philosopher Seneca says, “Luck happens when preparation meets opportunity.” In 2016, a doctoral candidate at the University of California Irvine proved that this is indeed the truth. Ten years ago, Mya Le Thai, PhD was playing around in the lab when she made a colossal discovery that could lead to a rechargeable battery capable of lasting up to 400 years. That means longer-lasting appliances, laptops, smartphones, cars and so much more, plus fewer lithium ion batteries piling up in landfills . A team of researchers at UCI had been experimenting with nanowires for potential use in batteries, but found that, over time, the thin fragile wires would break down and crack after too many charging cycles. A charge cycle is when a battery goes from completely full to completely empty and back to full again. Phone charging. Photo credit: Canva How the accidental discovery happened But one day on a whim, Thai coated a set of gold nanowires in manganese dioxide and a Plexiglas-like electrolyte gel. “She started to cycle these gel capacitors, and that’s when we got the surprise,” said Reginald Penner, chair of the university’s chemistry department . “She said, ‘this thing has been cycling 10,000 cycles and it’s still going.’ She came back a few days later and said ‘it’s been cycling for 30,000 cycles.’ That kept going on for a month.” This discovery is mind-blowing because the average laptop battery lasts 300 to 500 charge cycles. The nanobattery developed at UCI made it though 200,000 cycles in three months . That would extend the life of the average laptop battery by about 400 years. The rest of the device would have probably gone kaput decades before the battery, but the implications for a battery that lasts hundreds of years are pretty startling. “Mya was playing around, and she coated this whole thing with a very thin gel layer and started to cycle it,” Penner added. “She discovered that just by using this gel, she could cycle it hundreds of thousands of times without losing any capacity.” “That was crazy,” he added, “because these things typically die in dramatic fashion after 5,000 or 6,000 or 7,000 cycles at most.” “The big picture is that there may be a very simple way to stabilize nanowires of the type that we studied,” Penner said. “If this turns out to be generally true, it would be a great advance for the community.” Not bad for just fooling around in the laboratory! Where Mya Le Thai is today Since her discovery, Mya Le Thai earned her PhD and has gone on to a successful career as the Principal Scientist with the Enevate Corporation, a company set “to develop innovative battery technologies that accelerate adoption of electrified mobility,” according to their website. She has also filed patents for her various inventions, the most recent of which being “Cells with blocking devices for delayed heat propagation” in July 2025. As for the original nanowire battery discovery itself, it remains, nearly a decade later, a laboratory proof-of-concept rather than a commercial product. The gold nanowires that made the breakthrough possible are also prohibitively expensive at scale, a hurdle that would need to be solved (researchers have suggested nickel as a cheaper substitute) before this kind of battery could ever show up in an actual laptop or phone. Her full list of patents can be found on Justia . This article originally appeared ten years ago. It has been updated. The post A student accidentally created a rechargeable battery that she says could last 400 years appeared first on Upworthy .

Ναι, όλοι βλέπουμε πόσο χαριτωμένα είναι σε φωτογραφίες και βίντεο, αλλά το να ερωτεύεσαι, στην πραγματική ζωή, με ένα δικό σου γατάκι είναι ένα εντελώς άλλο επίπεδο απελπισίας. Κάθε πράγμα που κάνουν είναι χαριτωμένο. Κάθε χασμουρητό. Κάθε τέντωμα. Κάθε βόλτα. Μην με βάζεις καν να ξεκινήσω…
items.descriptionOriginal: It’s hard to explain the all-consuming adorableness of a kitten to someone who’s never had one. Yes, we all see how cute they are in photos and videos, but falling in love, in real life , with a kitten of your own is a whole other level of swoon. Every single thing they do is cute. Every yawn. Every stretch. Every pounce. Don’t even get me started on sneezes. How many times have we seen the classic “didn’t want a cat” story of a “not a cat person” falling hard and fast for a kitten? It happens. And a viral video of a man who is unable to contain himself over his new kitten’s cuteness perfectly encapsulates what that looks like. “Well, I’m just going to explode, aren’t I?” the man says to the woman behind the camera before going on and on about how he’d step in front of a bullet for the kitten. “Look at that cute little boy,” he says as the small orange tabby lies curled up in a blanket. “Yeah, that’s mine forever now. That’s mine forever. And he comes before you, now. He’s mine.” The pacing around with energy to burn. The “cute patootie bobooty.” The “I’m literally going to explode” moving right into the “I’m going to eat him,” and “I would die for you.” The fact that they just met and he’s already up to his eyeballs in gushy, smushy love. It’s all so relatable to those of us who’ve gone off the deep end after adding a tiny furry feline to our family. Cat owners immediately felt seen People in the comments shared the sentiment. “I got a kitten a week ago and it literally pains me to leave her everyday. She’s all i think about “ “The overstimulated pacing is so real.” “Every second of this was the correct response.” “I just got two and the overload of emotions is beyond words.” “12 years later and I still talk about my cat like this “ “The amount of times I tell her ‘I’d shmurder for you!!'” “The cuteness aggression is completely appropriate! ‘Cutie-patootie-bobootie, I’m gonna eat em.'” Grrrr, wook at his widdle paws and his widdle whiskers. Photo credit: Canva Cute aggression is a real thing Lots of people mentioned “cuteness aggression” in the comments, and that’s exactly what we’re witnessing in the video. When you feel so overwhelmed by the cuteness of something that you want to squish it, squeeze it, bite it, or even eat it? That’s cute aggression, a term coined by social psychologist Oriana Aragon in 2014 . “Cute aggression seems to be a mechanism to manage the overload of positive feelings we can get when we interact with something too cute for us to handle,” says Associate Professor Lisa A. Williams , a social psychologist from the University of New South Wales. “In other words, to counter an overwhelming barrage of positive feelings, we seek to tamp it down, and weirdly enough, that can play out as an aggressive inclination.” It’s not actually aggression in the strictest sense, as the impulse comes along with a strong feeling of wanting to protect the cute little animal, child, or whatever is causing the explosion of feeling. Like, you might feel a strong urge to bite your baby, but you would never actually bite your baby. You might want to squish your kitten or hug your puppy as tight as you can, but you wouldn’t because you know it would harm them. It’s a weird contrast of feelings, but it’s common. And it’s hard to explain to people who don’t experience it. Interestingly, Aragon says that those who do experience cute aggression also tend to experience other dimorphous expressions of positive emotion, which includes crying when happy. “People who, you know, want to pinch the baby’s cheeks and growl at the baby are also people who are more likely to cry at the wedding or cry when the baby’s born or have nervous laughter,” she told NPR . Whatever we call it, the urge to bite the baby or squish the kitten is real for many of us who feel totally seen in these videos. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Man’s inability to control himself over his new kitten’s cuteness is beyond relatable appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: In 1998, The Bee Gees , brothers Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb, stopped by ITV’s “Des O’Connor Tonight” with acoustic guitars in hand to promote their recent release, “One Night Only,” an album and live concert DVD featuring many of the band’s biggest hits . The highlight of the performance was when Barry got ready to strum his guitar for a performance of “How Deep Is Your Love,” the 1977 megahit from the “Saturday Night Fever Soundtrack,” but instead chose to sing the song a cappella. Their signature sound Barry starts the song solo in his beautiful falsetto, but then, when his brothers join him, they create a wonderful harmony that only brothers can make. The show’s host, Des O’Connor, a notable singer himself, even joins in for a few bars. Earlier in the performance, the brothers played their version of “Islands in the Stream,” a song made famous by Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers in 1983 that was written by the Bee Gees. In 1998, the song was enjoying a resurgence as its melody was used in the song “Ghetto Supastar” by Pras of The Fugees. Writing for music icons Robin Gibb later admitted that the song was initially written for Marvin Gaye to sing, but he was tragically murdered in 1984 by his father. The band also had Diana Ross in mind while composing the tune. During the appearance, the band also sang “Guilty,” a song that the Bee Gees wrote for Barbara Streisand and Barry produced in 1980. You can watch the entire performance here: The Gibb brothers started making music together when they were children, and after their first public appearance together at a local movie theater in 1956, they were hooked on performing. “It was the feeling of standing in front of an audience that was so amazing,” said Barry . “We’d never seen anything like it. We were very young, but it made an enormous impression. We didn’t want to do anything else but make music.” After the family moved to Australia in 1958, Barry, Maurice, and Robin were “discovered” at the Redcliffe Speedway, where they had asked to perform between races. Even over the tinny PA system, their harmonies made an impression. Speedway manager Bill Goode introduced the trio to DJ Bill Gates, who set them up with a recording session. From a land down under If you’ve ever wondered how the Bee Gees got their name, that was it: Bill Goode, Bill Gates, Barry Gibb, and the brothers’ mother Barbara Gibb all had the initials B.G. After a strong reception on the airwaves in Brisbane, Gates forwarded the brothers’ recordings to a Sydney radio station. They got a lot of airtime there as well, and the band had a run of success performing in Australia, but it wasn’t until their return to England in 1967 that they became the international sensation we all know today. Manager Robert Stigwood had received tapes from the Gibbs brothers and called them up within weeks of their arrival in the U.K. “I loved their composing,” Stigwood told Rolling Stone in 1977 . “I also loved their harmony singing. It was unique, the sound they made; I suppose it was a sound only brothers could make.” More than just disco And, as they say, the rest is history. The award-winning 2020 HBO documentary , “The Bee Gees: How Can You Mend a Broken Heart” tells the story of the band with loads of footage from throughout their 40-year career, which includes not only their disco-era fame, but the various phases of their musical journey and the countless songs they wrote for other artists. As one commenter wrote, “People that call the Bee Gees a ‘disco group’ don’t have a clue. They had 10 albums out before they ventured into ‘disco.’ Their song catalogue is amazing and some of their very best songs were written long before Saturday Night Fever. Those ‘disco’ songs are classics as well. It is nice to see they are finally getting the recognition they deserve.” This article originally appeared 1 year ago. It has been updated. items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News How Safer Driving Techniques Can Benefit the Environment Reading Time: 2 minutes How Safer Driving Techniques Can Benefit the Environment Driving more safely doesn’t just benefit road users. Many of the habits associated with safer driving can also reduce a vehicle’s environmental impact by lowering fuel or energy consumption and cutting harmful emissions . While wider developments in vehicle technology and transport policy play an important role, individual driving habits remain part of the picture. How smoother driving can cut fuel use and emissions According to Energy Saving Trust, efficient driving techniques such as smooth acceleration, staying within speed limits and avoiding unnecessary braking can help reduce fuel consumption and emissions. This means anticipating traffic conditions and maintaining a steady speed wherever it’s safe and practical to do so. Frequent acceleration and harsh braking require more energy than gradual speed changes. In petrol and diesel vehicles, this typically means burning more fuel. In electric vehicles, it can increase battery consumption and reduce driving range. Why speed, braking and forward planning matter Safe driving is closely linked to awareness and anticipation. Giving yourself more time to react to changing road conditions can help reduce sudden manoeuvres that increase fuel consumption and vehicle wear. For example, noticing traffic slowing ahead allows you to ease off the accelerator gradually instead of braking heavily at the last moment. Likewise, anticipating junctions and changing speed limits is key. Drivers looking to improve their awareness may find that utilising telematics insurance to help you be more aware of your driving style encourages more consistent habits, as many telematics systems monitor factors such as braking, acceleration and cornering behaviour. Look after the vehicle as well as your driving style Environmentally responsible driving is not solely about behaviour behind the wheel. Keeping your vehicle in good mechanical condition can also support efficiency and help emissions-control systems operate as intended. Regular servicing allows potential issues to be identified before they affect vehicle performance. Maintaining correct tyre pressures can reduce rolling resistance, while replacing worn components when required can help the vehicle run more efficiently. Drivers should also address dashboard warning lights promptly and ensure emissions-related components are functioning correctly. A poorly maintained vehicle may consume more fuel or energy than necessary. Motoring experts regularly highlight the importance of maintenance as part of environmentally conscious driving, alongside habits such as reducing unnecessary vehicle weight and keeping tyres correctly inflated. Put greener driving into the UK’s bigger environmental picture The UK’s transition towards lower-emission transport involves multiple factors, including advances in vehicle technology and public policy. However, driver behaviour still plays a role. If millions of motorists adopt more efficient driving habits, the combined effect can contribute to lower fuel consumption and reduced emissions across the vehicle fleet. While no individual action can solve environmental challenges on its own, small changes across a large population can support wider sustainability goals. The post How Safer Driving Techniques Can Benefit the Environment appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News How Retail LMS Software Can Support Training Across Store Teams Reading Time: 3 minutes How Retail LMS Software Can Support Training Across Store Teams Retail teams work across different stores, shifts, and job roles, so training must stay accessible during busy working days. Sales associates need product knowledge, supervisors need management guidance, and every employee must complete required safety courses. A dependable training platform helps meet these demands without disrupting daily store operations. A Learning Management System (LMS) brings these needs into one trackable program. The right retail LMS software also gives leaders a clearer view of participation, assessment results, and unresolved gaps, creating a practical foundation for consistent store training. The following areas outline what to consider when choosing a system. Create One Training Hub For Every Store A retail LMS gives employees one place to access onboarding, product updates, customer service lessons, and compliance courses. A retail LMS software directory helps decision-makers compare systems built for retail requirements, including mobile access, short lessons, progress tracking, and reporting. Centralized content reduces inconsistent instructions between locations and lets training leaders update a course without distributing new files manually. Store teams also benefit from clear learning paths. A new sales associate can complete orientation, point-of-sale training, and product lessons in sequence. A department supervisor can follow a separate path covering coaching, scheduling, inventory procedures, and incident reporting. Deliver Training Around Store Schedules Retail employees rarely share the same hours, making classroom sessions difficult to coordinate. Mobile access lets employees complete assigned lessons between shifts, during scheduled training time, or at another approved location. Short lessons support this schedule. A five-minute module can explain a product feature, customer greeting standard, or safety procedure without removing an employee from the sales floor for a long session. Managers can assign content by role, location, or employment stage, so each learner receives relevant material. A Learning Management System also records completion automatically. Managers do not need separate spreadsheets for each store, which reduces manual follow-up and gives regional leaders a consistent record. Keep Product And Service Knowledge Current Retail information changes often. Product lines, prices, promotions, return rules, and service expectations require regular updates. A central course library lets training teams revise a lesson once and publish the current version across selected stores. Knowledge checks give managers more than a completion mark. Short quizzes can test whether employees understand product differences, warranty conditions, or escalation procedures. Assessment results show where a team needs a refresher before a new promotion begins. Store leaders can also use assigned learning for seasonal hiring. Temporary employees receive the same essential service and safety information as permanent staff, with a clear deadline before their first scheduled shift. Track Compliance Without Manual Chasing Retail organizations must monitor courses related to workplace safety, data protection, harassment prevention, and other internal requirements. An LMS records assignments, due dates, completions, and assessment results in one system. Automated reminders help employees address overdue courses before managers need to contact each person. Escalation reports show which store, role, or department needs attention. These records also give training leaders evidence that required instruction was assigned and completed. Access controls support accurate reporting. A district manager can review assigned stores, while a store manager sees the employees within that location. This structure keeps reports useful without giving every user access to unnecessary information. Use Reports To Improve Store Performance Completion data helps leaders measure participation, but useful reporting goes further. Scores, attempts, time spent, and course status reveal whether employees understood the material or rushed through it. Training leaders can compare results by location or role to find recurring gaps. If several stores perform poorly on a product assessment, the lesson needs clearer explanations or better examples. If one location has low completion rates, managers can review scheduling, communication, or access problems. Learning data also supports regular management routines. Regional leaders can review a monthly report, discuss overdue assignments with store managers, and adjust upcoming training according to business needs. Give Managers A Practical Coaching Tool An LMS supports daily coaching when managers connect online lessons with store activity. After an employee completes a customer service module, a supervisor can observe a customer interaction and discuss the result privately. Managers can assign refresher lessons after an observed gap. They can also recognize completed development paths during one-on-one meetings and use assessment results to plan the next coaching conversation. This approach keeps training connected to job behavior. Employees receive instruction, practice the skill, and discuss progress with a manager instead of treating courses as isolated administrative tasks. Conclusion Retail LMS software gives store teams a shared training structure without forcing every employee into the same schedule. The strongest implementation starts with role-based learning paths, mobile-friendly lessons, current product content, and compliance tracking. Training leaders should audit existing courses, group them by role and store need, then select a system that reports completion and assessment results clearly. A small pilot across several locations provides useful evidence before wider deployment. The post How Retail LMS Software Can Support Training Across Store Teams appeared first on Happy Eco News .
